bib.title: Appendix A: Context Engine Reference Guide (Context Engineering for Multi-Agent Systems)

question: How is the book's Context Engine (Planner/Executor, MCP-message agents, RAG over a knowledge store and a blueprint library, safeguards) structured, function by function, so a reader can build and maintain it?
contributions: Function-level reference for helpers.py, agents.py, registry.py, engine.py, utils.py
Description of the data ingestion pipeline and the control deck
Three workflow templates and a layered safeguard design (sanitization, two-stage moderation, policy meta-controller)

limits: No experiments, measurements or evaluation; all statements are design description and assertion (e.g. 'glass-box', 'pioneers RAG for procedural retrieval' are unsupported claims).
Several values are marked 'e.g.' (chunk 400, overlap 50, model gpt-5, text-embedding-3-small); injection pattern list is only illustrated, and regex matching is a weak defense.
Authors concede LLM stochasticity remains and output varies between runs; latency is the trade-off of multi-step planning.
Code is not reproduced in the appendix; no authors printed in the PDF; mentions Gemini 2.5 Pro Ultra as current at time of writing, which has dated.
practices: Vet user goals before execution and generated output after it with a moderation call that fails safe (returns flagged on API error) (Production safeguards; helper_moderate_content).
Sanitize every retrieved chunk against known injection patterns before synthesis and skip tainted chunks (Input sanitization).
Store chunk text and source filename as vector metadata so answers carry verifiable citations (Data ingestion, step 4).
Retrieve procedural context (semantic blueprints, embedded by their intent description) separately from factual context, using two namespaces (Context Librarian, Ingesting the context library).
Have the Planner emit a JSON plan with $$STEP_N_OUTPUT$$ placeholders and resolve them in the Executor to chain context between agents (planner, resolve_dependencies).
Inject only the dependencies each agent needs via a registry factory, and give the Planner an auto-generated capabilities description (AgentRegistry).
Use a Summarizer agent as a gatekeeper to reduce context and control token cost; count tokens with tiktoken, falling back to cl100k_base (agent_summarizer, count_tokens).
Log plan, planned vs resolved inputs, outputs, status and duration in an execution trace for debugging (ExecutionTrace).
Keep deterministic business rules in a policy-driven meta-controller above the engine that assembles the control deck, instead of growing engine code (Policy-driven solution).
Expect output variation between runs of identical goals (Operational realities).

terms.definition: a multi-agent system, orchestrated by a Planner and Executor communicating via MCP, that is the practical implementation of context engineering
a structured, unambiguous plan provided to the LLM, typically in JSON format. It defines the goal of the generation, the style guide, the structure, and the roles of the participants
the vector database (Pinecone namespace ContextLibrary) holding semantic blueprints, retrieved by the Context Librarian
execution trace exposes every step of reasoning so failures can be located in planning, retrieval, sanitization or generation
standardized message dict with protocol_version, sender, content, metadata, built by create_mcp_message
the Executor passes the output of one agent as input to the next via resolve_dependencies and $$STEP_N_OUTPUT$$ placeholders
the interactive notebook cell where the engineer defines goal, config and execution (optionally with moderation)
a higher-level application above the Context Engine that parses input, enforces policy and assembles the control deck
